title: CTF flag submissions do not consistently share the report caps and cooldown policy

original_titles.title: CTF flag submissions bypass caps and cooldowns

problem: The generic submission path branches CTF flags into verify_flag work before the same bug-report cap/cooldown controls, so flags can bypass limits applied to normal reports. The exact policy must distinguish per-flag max_awards from per-user/team submission rate limits.
impact: A participant can brute-force flag submissions or generate disproportionate verification load even if flag awards are capped.

verification.basis: Current source inspection at the main-branch commit listed in metadata. Original audit line numbers are treated as historical and were not reused as current line references.

implementation_steps.action: Define per-user, per-team, per-stage and per-IP flag submission caps independently from award max_awards.
Apply cooldown/rate limits before enqueuing verify_flag and record failed attempts without revealing whether a particular flag key exists.
Use idempotency and a unique submission record so duplicate/replayed flags cannot enqueue unbounded work.
Add brute-force, duplicate, parallel and cross-team flag tests.

acceptance_criteria: Flags obey a documented rate/cap policy.
Invalid flag attempts reveal no oracle and do not flood the worker queue.
regression_tests: Add a focused failing test before implementation where practical.
Add a negative authorization / boundary test, not only a happy-path test.
Run the affected backend/frontend suite and the full CI workflow before merge.
